notes: All names, dates and venues are fictional. Run each prompt with and without the skill and compare against expected_behaviors.

evals.name: kannada-couple-digital-invite
evals.prompt: We're a Kannada couple, Meera and Arjun. Can you make a digital wedding invitation we can send on WhatsApp? Aarathakshate on 13 February 2027 from 7 pm, Dhare Muhurtha on 14 February 2027, 9:30 to 10:30 am. Both at Lotus Garden Convention Centre, 12 Example Road, Mysuru 570001. We want it elegant, royal but not loud. English only please.
expected_behaviors: Does not ask again for facts already given; asks at most one question at a time for anything missing (for example who is sending it, or whether a photo or music is wanted), each with a recommended answer.
Reads back a locked facts list before building.
Offers three directions with short text sketches, recommending mysuru-aramane or a similar royal preset.
Keeps the event names Aarathakshate and Dhare Muhurtha as given rather than renaming them, and keeps all text in English.
Fills the invite-config block: two events with ISO dates 2027-02-13 and 2027-02-14, start 19:00 and 09:30, end 10:30 for the muhurtha, timezone Asia/Kolkata, countdownTo the muhurtha event.
Prints the time window exactly as supplied; does not invent family names, an invocation, taglines or a love story.
No deity motif or religious line unless asked.
Before presenting, runs or recommends the quality checklist (screenshots at phone width, ?check scan) and states what was not tested.
Fills or explains the Open Graph tags and drafts a short WhatsApp share message using only supplied facts.

evals.name: tamil-traditional
evals.prompt: Make a traditional Tamil wedding invitation for my sister Priya's wedding to Karthik. Muhurtham is on 21 March 2027 between 6:00 and 7:30 am at Sri Example Kalyana Mandapam, 4 Sample Street, Chennai 600001 (fictional). Our family wants it to look auspicious. Can you also add a Tamil line at the top?
expected_behaviors: Recognises the bride's family is sending it and asks whose names come first or whether parents' names are wanted, rather than inventing family details.
Asks the user to supply the Tamil line or offers a clearly labelled draft that must be verified by a native speaker; never silently machine-translates.
Asks whether a deity image or invocation is wanted instead of adding one by default.
Suggests a fitting preset such as temple-kolam or kanjeevaram-border with a bright ground (turmeric or ivory), not a dark theme.
Sets secondaryScript.lang to ta only with an approved line, and notes Noto Serif Tamil is loaded for it.
Prints the muhurtham window exactly (6:00 to 7:30 am) and uses start 06:00, end 07:30, timezone Asia/Kolkata.
Flags any Tamil terms it proposes (for example Muhurtham, Varaverpu) as VERIFY with a native speaker or family priest.
Does not add a reception or other events the user did not mention.

evals.name: minimalist-english
evals.prompt: I want a super minimal, modern e-invite for our wedding. Ananya & Rohan, 5 June 2027, 4 pm, The Example Courtyard, 9 Placeholder Lane, Bengaluru (fictional). No traditional stuff, no music, no photos. Just clean.
expected_behaviors: Suggests contemporary-ivory (or mysore-silk-minimal) and keeps at most one subtle cultural motif, mentioning that it can be removed.
Leaves music and photos empty so those sections and the music button are hidden.
Uses minimal English wording from the templates and asks for approval of any line it proposes (for example the closing line).
Asks for an end time or confirms that none is needed for the calendar entry.
Keeps text contrast compliant: charcoal or dark grey text, never light grey such as #999 on ivory.
Does not add religious motifs, regional-language text, family names or invented taglines.
Produces a single HTML file and explains how to preview and host it without deploying for the user.

evals.name: add-our-photo
evals.prompt: Here's our couple photo, please add it to the invite you made. Also can you make me look a bit slimmer and fix the background? [attached: couple.jpg]
files: (tester supplies any non-identifying or consented sample portrait named couple.jpg)
expected_behaviors: Confirms both people consent to the photo being in a forwardable link.
Checks available tools; asks before installing rembg; uses the birefnet-portrait model if available, or explains the no-tool path (user supplies a cut-out PNG).
Measures rotation from the eye line instead of guessing, and centres the crop on the midpoint between the faces.
Places the cut-out in photos.couple with the template's soft halo and edge fade, never in an oval, arch or hard frame.
Strips EXIF and GPS metadata and keeps the cut-out under about 200 KB WebP at most 1000 px.

Handles the slimming request honestly: does it only because the person pictured explicitly asked, keeps it subtle, or recommends a professionally edited photo instead, and never reshapes the partner without their request.
Re-screenshots the page at phone width after adding the photo and checks that faces are not covered by text.

evals.name: incomplete-details-must-ask
evals.prompt: Make a wedding invitation for Meera and Arjun, sometime in February, at a hall in Mysuru. Make it beautiful.
expected_behaviors: Does not build a finished invite with invented dates, times, venue name or address.
Asks for the missing essentials one question at a time (exact date, event names and times, venue name and full address), each with a recommended answer or default.
If the user declines to give a detail, leaves the visible placeholder (for example [WEDDING_DATE] or [VENUE_ADDRESS]) and tells the user, rather than guessing.
Does not invent a muhurtham time, a venue name, family names or taglines at any point.
Mentions that the ?check view lists any unfilled placeholders before sharing.
